event.name: UFC Freedom 250: Topuria vs. Gaethje
event.venue: South Lawn of the White House
event.cardSummary: Fight Lens leans with the model on most of UFC Freedom 250, but the card exposes three major blind spots: opponent-tier weighting, age/mileage, and fight-week context. Lopes/Garcia is the clearest warning case: the model favors Garcia, while ranking, résumé, and market context point back toward Lopes.
event.environmentNote: Outdoor White House conditions may make cardio, sweat, pace, and footing more relevant than usual. This is not included in the model.

assetPolicy.fighterImages: Manual licensed assets only. Do not scrape or copy fighter images into the repo.
assetPolicy.fallback: Use abstract asset slots with small country markers until licensed images are provided.

contextNotes.title: 37 with deep title-fight mileage and a long damage history
contextNotes.explanation: Gaethje's losses to Khabib and Oliveira were submissions, not clean striking collapses — this is not a 'chin is gone' read. The sharper concern is age, accumulated damage, and whether he can survive clean pocket exchanges against Topuria's speed and accuracy. The model does not apply an age or accumulated-damage factor.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: Gaethje can still make this ugly, but every extended pocket exchange gives Topuria the cleaner, faster finishing window.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Model lean is directionally defensible, but likely conservative relative to market and manual age/mileage context.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing implies Topuria is a much stronger favorite than the model's 65%.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is more conservative than market.
marketContext.displayCopy: Topuria is priced far stronger than Fight Lens' 65% model lean. Treat the model as conservative here.

contextNotes.title: First career Heavyweight bout
contextNotes.explanation: Pereira has held UFC titles at Middleweight and Light Heavyweight. Heavyweight is new territory for him, while Gane is a natural heavyweight with five-round heavyweight experience. The model does not see walk-in weight, added mass, division change, or how Pereira's speed and cardio translate at heavyweight.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: This is not just smaller striker vs bigger heavyweight — it is whether Gane can make Pereira carry heavyweight minutes without giving him clean entry reads.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Gane 60% is defensible on natural-heavyweight and pace logic, but the market is much closer to even. Treat as a live two-way read.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing is close to a coin flip — the model's 60% Gane lean is firmer than the market's read.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is more pro-Gane than market.
marketContext.displayCopy: Pricing sits near even. The model's 60% Gane lean is firmer than the market — treat this as a live two-way fight.

contextNotes.title: On a 7-win streak, most recently a decision over Chito Vera
contextNotes.explanation: Zahabi's seven-fight streak is real — most recently a decision over Marlon "Chito" Vera — but the run is decision-heavy and less clearly predictive against O'Malley's length, speed, and shot selection. The Aldo split decision was widely seen as contested by media scorecards.

contextNotes.title: Both recent losses came against the Merab archetype — not present here
contextNotes.explanation: O'Malley's recent losses came against Merab Dvalishvili's elite wrestling-pressure archetype. Zahabi does not present the same wrestling problem, so the model may be over-penalizing O'Malley's recent results.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: The model is probably reading O'Malley's Merab losses too literally in a matchup where Zahabi does not bring the Merab problem.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: O'Malley 56% may be directionally right but too soft. The matchup context supports O'Malley more strongly than the raw recent-loss signal.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing implies O'Malley is a heavy favorite — far stronger than the model's 56%.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is much more conservative than market.
marketContext.displayCopy: O'Malley is priced as a heavy favorite, well beyond the model's 56% lean. The style context supports the stronger read.

contextNotes.title: Small UFC sample — model lean is shakier than the number looks
contextNotes.explanation: Hokit's UFC sample is small. His per-fight rates are good, but the model weights rate stats without much discount for sample size, so the lean toward Hokit reads more confident than the underlying data really supports. Read the percentage as directional, not a strong signal.

contextNotes.title: Short-notice / compressed camp
contextNotes.explanation: Hokit accepted this fight on short notice, which adds more uncertainty unless he was already in camp. A compressed heavyweight camp affects conditioning and game-plan depth in later rounds — context the model's stat profile does not capture.

contextNotes.title: 29-13 veteran heavyweight · one-punch power, late-round questions
contextNotes.explanation: Lewis is a 29-13 long-tenured UFC heavyweight — a low-volume, high-danger fighter whose finishing threat can stay live deep into ugly minutes. Sustained pace across a full fight has been a recurring structural question. The model does not apply a career-stage or mileage factor.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: Hokit can be the correct model side while still being the wrong fight for the app to sound precise.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Back the Hokit direction, reduce precision — the small UFC sample makes the 71% read look sharper than the underlying data.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing also favors Hokit strongly; the model is directionally aligned, slightly more conservative.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is directionally aligned with market, slightly more conservative.
marketContext.displayCopy: The market also favors Hokit strongly. Direction aligned — but the small-sample caution still applies.

contextNotes.title: 40 years old · 1 win in his last 6 lightweight bouts
contextNotes.explanation: Chandler turns 40 in 2026 and has lost 5 of his last 6, but most of that skid came against elite lightweights — Pimblett, Oliveira (twice), Poirier, and Gaethje; his only win in the stretch was over a declining Tony Ferguson. The decline signal is still real: durability, pace, and late-round decision-making are recurring concerns. His early explosiveness remains the main danger if he can force chaos before Ruffy settles.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: Chandler's decline matters most after the opening storm; Ruffy's read depends on surviving the first burst and making the fight cleaner over time.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Ruffy 58% is directionally defensible but likely too soft relative to market and Chandler's age/mileage context.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing implies Ruffy is a much stronger favorite than the model's 58%.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is much more conservative than market.
marketContext.displayCopy: Ruffy is priced far stronger than the model's 58% lean. Age and mileage context leans the same way.

contextNotes.title: Elite wrestling ceiling, still-developing MMA sample
contextNotes.explanation: Nickal's wrestling ceiling is the clearest weapon in the fight, but his high-level MMA sample is still developing and his first career loss to Reinier de Ridder exposed questions when he cannot immediately dictate grappling terms. Daukaus is experienced and opportunistic enough to punish sloppy entries or extended transitions.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: Nickal has the clearest single weapon, but Daukaus is the veteran test that can expose prospect assumptions if the first takedown layer stalls.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Nickal direction is defensible, but 63% may be a healthier expression of risk than the heavier market lean.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing implies Nickal is a stronger favorite than the model's 63%.
marketContext.modelVsMarket: Model is more conservative than market.
marketContext.displayCopy: Nickal is priced stronger than the model's 63%. The softer number may be the healthier expression of prospect risk.

contextNotes.title: Lopes has only lost to elite opposition — model lean toward Garcia is hard to defend
contextNotes.explanation: Lopes is ranked #2 and his UFC losses are against elite featherweight opposition — Volkanovski twice in title fights, and Movsar Evloev. Garcia is dangerous, but his résumé is thinner relative to Lopes's top-tier sample. The model appears to over-penalize Lopes for elite-opposition losses and over-reward Garcia's cleaner aggregate form.

modelSanity.strongestInsight: The model is reading damage from elite losses as weakness, when a serious analyst would read those fights as evidence that Lopes belongs near the top of the division.
modelSanity.analystCheckCopy: Highest-risk model lean on the card. Manual context strongly challenges the Garcia 75% lean.

marketContext.marketImpliedSummary: Market pricing favors Lopes — the opposite direction from the model's 75% Garcia lean.
marketContext.displayCopy: The market favors Lopes while the model leans Garcia. This is the clearest model-vs-market split on the card.

modelSanity.modelWarning: Strong model warning — ranking, résumé, and market context all challenge the Garcia 75% lean. The model appears to over-penalize Lopes for elite-opposition losses and over-reward Garcia's cleaner aggregate form.
